instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Back Me Up
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to support your version of how an ordinary responsibility should be handled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll chair the house meeting. Back my proposal that Alex takes the bins tonight and we'll get it settled calmly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's your turn. Alex did last week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then my proposal includes me doing the washing-up. Would that make it a fair exchange in your view?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if Alex gets to say no. I'll support asking, not announcing it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, a consultation. You introduce the option in your words and I'll chair the discussion. Just make sure they hear it's a sensible way to divide the work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle the manager. You back me up that I agreed to cover the morning, not the evening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wasn't in that meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine, stick to what you know. Tell her you saw me put the morning shift in my calendar. I'll lead the explanation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saw you typing. I couldn't see the screen, and I won't pretend I could.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Quite right; accuracy is how we'll handle this. Say you saw me checking my calendar after the meeting. If that's too much, just stand beside me while I explain the morning arrangement.

cards.title: Try It First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've fixed the tap. We'll do this properly: you turn it on, then I'll start the washing-up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Last time your fix sprayed me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which is why I'm supervising this test with a raincoat. You can wear it, and choose how far to open the tap.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You hold a bucket under that joint. Then I'll turn it on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the controlled test I had in mind. Choose the bucket; I'll hold it. Run the water before we put any dishes underneath. Tell me when you're ready.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've sorted our breakfast budget. Taste this coffee substitute and then I'll fill my cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We have proper coffee. I want that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're our quality check. If you say no, we keep the proper coffee. I'm not imposing anything that doesn't work for us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want a croissant for doing your quality check.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A proper tasting breakfast, exactly. Choose the croissant; I'll pay. One sip before I fill my cup, and you decide whether my new budget needs revising.

cards.title: Count What I Did
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the practical work, time, or inconvenience you contributed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've got the shopping organized. Twelve bags up six flights; let's make sure nobody calls that a quick shop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I won't. Sit down and I'll put it all away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, that's the recovery plan. Put it wherever suits you. The peas came up on a separate trip, though.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then have two rests. I'll bring tea after the first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Could you say 'tea for the second trip' when you bring it? Quietly is fine. I just don't want my well-managed recovery mistaken for one long sit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fence finished. I'll give you the proper account: my whole Saturday went into those three panels.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They look good. I'll tell next door; they need six done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them I planned two shop trips and drove eighteen screws. It wasn't a spare half-hour. Use your own words, obviously.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll just say you worked hard. I'm not reciting a tool list over the fence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A concise account, good. Say I worked hard all Saturday. That's the bit I need them to hear before they ask about Sunday.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've got dinner and your departure organized. Choose now: I stir your parents' gravy or drive you to the station.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you put dinner on a timer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The timer won't stir it. But I'm flexible about the order: which job do you want first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Gravy. I'll book a taxi. Just bring my suitcase downstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, transport sorted. I'll fit in the case if that's your priority. Shall I carry it now and let the gravy lump, or keep stirring while you bring it down?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm coordinating the pickups. Your mum is at the station; her birthday parcel is at the depot that shuts at six. Which comes first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Get Mum. She hates waiting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum first, exactly. Then you can tell her the present stays locked up tonight. Would you prefer the parcel first instead?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Get the parcel. I'll keep Mum company on the phone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good teamwork; that's the route. She's ringing me now, though. You decide: I stop to explain we're following your plan, or keep driving and leave her call unanswered?

cards.title: Move It for Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to rearrange an ordinary commitment as proof that your relationship takes priority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've planned lunch for us at one. Move the haircut; your oldest friend gets that slot today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've had that appointment for weeks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I've had you since school. You choose where we eat; I just want to know I can outrank a trim.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Changing it today costs twenty pounds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll cover that. A proper friendship budget. You pick lunch, I'll follow your lead. Just cross out the haircut and write my name in its place while I'm here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've arranged my exhibition opening so you can come tonight. Tell the quiz team their captain is leaving early for his sister.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They need me through the first round. I can't just abandon them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll keep the welcome until after round one. I can manage that. Tell them family comes next.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll come then, but I'll say I've got a headache. Less fuss.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine, no announcement. Tell just the teammate beside you that you're coming for me. I'll move my whole welcome for you; let me at least outrank a headache.
